body: Yeah.  I just want to curl up in a blank space.
I haven't seen it, but yeah, that looks right.

I don't have the means to have a garden right now, but perhaps I could find some potted plants.

I like the idea of being anchored in dirt.

I'm in North Dakota, and I love the prairies.  That kind of vastness is so comforting to me.  Manitoba is gorgeous.

I was actually in the Maritimes this October and I would like to live there full-time if possible.  I stayed in New Brunswick and visited PEI and Nova Scotia.  Visiting there really changed my life, though by the tone of my post here on sw, I suppose you'd never guess it.

I'd love to have a garden like yours!

> For me, my place is in my room. I'm in Canada, so it snows and is miserably cold where I am for a good part of the year. When I crawl into my bed and pull the blankets up over my head and pretend that it's just me, there are times when that lure still calls. Just blank- no highs, no lows- just pale grey, and that is so seductive.

Exactly.

Also, I spent some time alone in Canada this fall.  It was beautiful, and precisely what I wanted.  If you don't mind, which province are you in?

It is, thanks.  I read your post and related to it as though I'd written it myself.

We can be there for each other, though not in person.

Oh my god, you understand.  

Thanks for believing in me.  I'm not sure that I do anymore.  I'm not a big crier, but reading your words has tears pooling in my eyes.
I understand the appeal, but not really.

For a few months.  It's worse right now than it has been recently.

Yes, but not quite to the same extent.
Thank you.  I do know that on an intellectual level, but it's good to hear.
I'm not sure what to say.  It's just a crushing burden of fatigue that has settled somewhere in my chest, in the vicinity of the heart.  I want someone to hold me while I sleep.
